1: Study design for the country-label application and its prompt assessment. (a) LSMS–ISA surveys supplied 490 profiles from seven African countries. (b) Four prompt designs were compared for 280 profiles from Ethiopia, Malawi, Nigeria and Tanzania using Claude, Codex and Kimi, yielding 3,360 responses. T1 provided the common format for the application. (c) The seven-country benchmark combined 840 shared T1 responses with 630 extension responses. In the paired experiment, the same 70 Tanzanian profiles received seven country labels, with other prompt fields fixed and administrative regions omitted. Its 1,470 records include 420 reused Tanzania- and Nigeria-label responses. An additional East Africa label contributed 210 responses. (d) Comparisons covered national estimates, individual agreement, trait associations and survey-weighted nitrogen quantities. The African analyses contain 5,670 distinct response records after accounting for shared calls.
2: Nitrogen prediction under four prompt designs in the African sample. (a) Pearson correlation, (b) mean absolute error (MAE), (c) distribution similarity, defined as one minus the two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic, and (d) the ratio of simulated to observed standard deviations (SD). All 12 interface–prompt configurations use the same 275 profiles with observed nitrogen rates. Dashed lines show the error from assigning each profile the observed median in (b), the archived distribution-only reference in (c), and equal simulated and observed SDs in (d). The distribution-only reference averages 400 samples of 280 values generated from a zero-inflated lognormal fitted to the 275 observed rates; values are assigned independently of farmer characteristics. Each point summarizes one accepted response per profile and condition, and lines connect T1–T4 within an interface.
